seo.description: Visiting Dar Sebti in Oujda? History of the restored palace, cultural events, Gharnati music, best time to go and how to include it in your itinerary.
seo.og_title: Dar Sebti, Oujda: Cultural Palace & Visit Tips
seo.og_description: A restored 20th-century palace that hosts cultural life and Gharnati music in the heart of Oujda.

name: Dar Sebti
hero_subtitle: A restored palace in Oujda that opens its doors to culture, architecture and the sound of Gharnati music.

overview.title: Architecture and Living Culture
overview.p1: Dar Sebti is a 20th-century palace that has been restored and given a new role as a cultural venue. Its architecture reflects the refined taste of its era, with courtyards, decorative details and spaces designed for gathering.
overview.p2: Today it is best known for hosting cultural events and performances of Gharnati music – the Andalusian-influenced classical tradition that is one of Oujda’s artistic treasures. Even when no concert is scheduled, the building itself rewards a short visit for its atmosphere and craftsmanship.
overview.p3: Because opening hours and access can depend on events, it is wise to ask locally or check recent information before making a special trip. When it is open, it offers a quieter, more refined counterpoint to the energy of the medina.

moods.title: When to Visit Dar Sebti
moods.subtitle: Access is often linked to the cultural calendar.

1.title: Concerts and Cultural Evenings
1.desc: The best time to experience the palace is during a Gharnati performance or public cultural event. The atmosphere becomes fully alive.

2.title: Architecture and Quiet
2.desc: When open for daytime visits, the courtyards and rooms offer a peaceful look at early-20th-century design and restoration work.

3.title: With the Park or Medina
3.desc: Pair a visit with Parc Lalla Aicha or a medina walk. The three together give a balanced picture of Oujda’s historic and living centre.

food.title: What to Eat Nearby
food.p1: Dar Sebti is in a central area with cafés and restaurants within walking distance.
food.li1: Mint tea or coffee on a nearby terrace after your visit.
food.li2: Simple grills and daily specials in the surrounding streets.
food.li3: Karan and barida if you walk toward the more traditional food zones.
food.li4: For an evening event, many visitors eat before or after in the modern centre.
food.li5: Ask the venue or your hotel for current restaurant recommendations close by.
food.p2: There is usually no restaurant inside the palace itself; plan to eat outside.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Dar Sebti

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Located in central Oujda and reachable by petit taxi or on foot from many hotels. Ask for “Dar Sebti” – it is a known cultural address.

2.title: Check Before You Go
2.desc: Opening depends on the programme. Confirm hours or event tickets locally, via your hotel, or through recent online information.

3.title: Etiquette
3.desc: Dress neatly for cultural events. Photography rules may vary; always follow staff instructions inside the building.

q1.question: Is Dar Sebti always open?
q1.answer: No. Access often depends on cultural events or organised visits. Check current information before you go.

q2.question: What is Gharnati music?
q2.answer: Gharnati is a classical musical tradition with strong Andalusian roots, particularly cultivated in Oujda and the Oriental region. Dar Sebti is one of the places where it is performed.

q3.question: How long should I spend at Dar Sebti?
q3.answer: 45 minutes to 1.5 hours depending on whether you are viewing the architecture or attending an event.

q4.question: Is there an entrance fee?
q4.answer: It varies. Some visits or events are free or low-cost; concerts may require tickets. Confirm locally.

q5.question: Can I combine it with other sights?
q5.answer: Yes. It sits well with a visit to Parc Lalla Aicha and the medina on the same day.
